text-tertiary.note: Default colour of MonoCaps and the most-read text in the app. Raised from #5C626D (2.9:1 on chrome) to clear 4.5:1 on every ground it lands on; 4.8:1 at worst.

text-disabled.note: 1.7:1 — deliberately below the text threshold, which makes it not a text colour. Disabled-control ink and dormant indicator fills only.

_scaling.purpose: Every size is scaled relative to the standard text style nearest its own value — 9-11pt tracks caption2, 12pt caption1, 13-14pt footnote, 15pt subheadline, 16pt callout, 17-19pt body, 20pt title3, 22-27pt title2, 28-33pt title1, 34pt+ largeTitle. The style is derived from the size inside LG.Font, so roles grow at different rates and no call site had to change. Floor of 9pt; the remote screen clamps at accessibility1 because its geometry is thumb-arc and video, not text.

_family.purpose: SF Mono and SF Pro. LG.Font.mono names IBM Plex Mono first but nothing bundles it — no UIAppFonts key, no font file — so the custom branch never executes today.

display.purpose: The Mac's own name on Home. Used once per screen, never for a label.

headline.purpose: The single sentence a full-screen moment turns on — pairing instruction, revoke consequence.

title.purpose: Screen titles and the label on a filled primary action.

body.purpose: All prose. 15pt primary, 13pt supporting. Never truncated.

label.purpose: Every heading, unit, status line and caption. Uppercased, tracked 0.8–4.4pt. The machine's voice.

readout.purpose: A measured value with its unit set smaller and dimmer. The atom the system is built from.

code.purpose: Tool names, paths, diff lines, verbatim commands. Selectable, never truncated mid-token.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Every state transition: selection, latch, expand, sheet. The default.

motion.name: rise
motion.value: move from bottom edge + opacity — opacity alone under Reduce Motion
motion.purpose: Bottom sheets: permission, revoke, modifier tray, keyboard bar, Claude panel, banner. LG.Motion.rise(reduced:).

motion.name: push
motion.value: move from trailing edge — opacity alone under Reduce Motion
motion.purpose: The settings screen. The longest travel in the app, so the clearest Reduce Motion case. LG.Motion.push(reduced:).

motion.name: hub-spring
motion.value: spring(response 280ms, damping 0.78), 18ms per-spoke stagger; ease-out 140ms with no scale under Reduce Motion
motion.purpose: The control hub's six spokes arriving along the thumb arc — the app's one authored moment. The stagger survives Reduce Motion because sequence is timing, not movement.

motion.name: condition-pulse-healthy
motion.purpose: Condition dot at a healthy link. Suppressed while video is live, and under Reduce Motion — it rests at full opacity, since colour and label already carry the condition.

motion.name: condition-pulse-degraded
motion.purpose: Condition dot on a thin link — a faster blink is the signal.

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: Running tool calls, exchange steps, stream opening. The one loop that keeps running under Reduce Motion: a small rotating arc is not a vestibular trigger, and a frozen spinner would claim the host stopped answering.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: Focused code box and the streaming indicator. Rests visible under Reduce Motion — a still caret still marks the position.

motion.name: travelling-dot
motion.purpose: The one motion on the pairing screen: a dot crossing the dashed line between the two machines. Rests at the midpoint under Reduce Motion; the discovery line below always carried the state in words.

motion.name: breathing-ring
motion.purpose: The trackpad teaching hint, retired after three sessions. Holds its outer radius under Reduce Motion rather than scaling out from a point.

breakpoints.name: portrait
breakpoints.value: height > width — stacked instrument, 96pt bottom bar

breakpoints.name: landscape
breakpoints.value: width > height — picture left, 231pt control dock right, status bar hidden

narrative.overview:
VibeWire is a gauge cluster for one machine. Every mark on the glass reports something that was actually measured — round-trip time, packet loss, megabits, the age of the last good frame, how long a tool has been waiting on an answer. Nothing on screen is decoration wearing the costume of information. When a value has not been measured, the panel prints an em dash and holds the space, because an unmeasured value and a measured zero are different facts and the interface is not allowed to blur them.

The room is dark and stays dark. There is no light mode, no colorScheme branching, and no shadow anywhere in the app. Depth is built from five tonal grounds and a one-point hairline, the way a bezel separates one dial from the next. Type does the second half of the work: monospace with wide tracking for anything counted or named by the machine, system sans for prose the user reads at their own pace. The two never trade jobs, so the eye learns in one screen which parts of the panel are readings and which are sentences.

Color is a signalling system with exactly four voices, and the most important thing about it is the split: jade, sodium and clay report what the Mac is doing, and cyan reports what the user is doing — a held modifier, an active selection, a Claude session, the caret. That separation is what lets a glance in a dark room distinguish "the link is degrading" from "I left Command switched on." It is rejected outright as a generic remote-desktop client with a gray toolbar and one undifferentiated "Connected", as a consumer chat app with bubbles and avatars, and as a neon hacker dashboard where color is atmosphere. The unhappy states — asleep, thin link, unreachable — are drawn with the same care as the happy one, because those are the states that cost the user two minutes.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only, five tonal grounds, zero shadows
Monospace for measured, sans for prose — never interchangeable
Four signal colors: three for the machine, one reserved for the user
Hairlines and tint-washes instead of cards
Every primary action states its own cost before it is tapped
Motion is 120–180 ms state change; nothing decorative moves beside live video

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Jade, sodium and clay describe the machine. Cyan describes the user. A control may never take a machine color to mean "on", and a condition may never take cyan to mean "bad". Any new color must declare which side of that line it lives on, or it does not get added.

rules.name: The Dash Rule
rules.body: A value that has not been measured renders as an em dash in Text Disabled at the same size the real value will take. Never 0, never blank, never a spinner in place of a number.

rules.name: The Measured Condition Rule
rules.body: Condition is derived from measured inputs (Condition.from(rttMillis:lossPercent:awake:)), never set by hand at a call site. The label and the numbers beside it cannot disagree, because they come from the same expression.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: A text colour is chosen by computing it against the ground it actually lands on — and against the lightest such ground, not the average. Dark is a product decision here, so there is no light appearance to fall back on and the palette has to carry legibility by itself. Body and label text clears 4.5:1; anything that cannot is not a text colour.

rules.name: The No Alpha Over Video Rule
rules.body: Nothing readable sits on the Mac's picture as translucent ink. Alpha over content nobody controls has no contrast ratio — white at 34% measures 2.9:1 over a black desktop and 1.0:1 over a white document. Marks over video are solid and carry their own ground (.videoChip()).

rules.name: The Two Registers Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for anything the machine measured or named: values, units, paths, keys, commands, statuses. Sans is for anything written to be read as language. A label never becomes sans to look friendlier, and prose never becomes mono to look technical.

rules.name: The Verbatim Rule
rules.body: A command, a path, or an error the user may need to act on is rendered mono, selectable, and never truncated mid-token. Truncation, when unavoidable, takes the head of a path and the middle of a target — never the tail that carries the filename.

rules.name: The Held Space Rule
rules.body: A layout does not move when a value arrives. Pending values are drawn as a dashed rule or an em dash occupying the final geometry, so filling in is a substitution rather than a reflow.

rules.name: The Whole Glass Rule
rules.body: On the remote screen the input surface is the full frame, including the letterbox bands. Anything drawn over the picture is non-hit-testing unless it is itself a control.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from tone and a hairline. If two surfaces are not separable, the fix is a hairline or a ground step — never a shadow, never a blur.

rules.name: The Tint Means Condition Rule
rules.body: A colored panel wash (5% fill, 30% border) is reserved for a panel that is reporting that condition. It is never used to make an ordinary container look interesting.

rules.name: The Dashed-Is-Provisional Rule
rules.body: Dashed means unmeasured, pending, or unselected. It resolves to a solid stroke the moment the thing becomes real. Dashes are never used decoratively.

rules.name: The Preflight Rule
rules.body: A primary action always states, in its own sub-label, what it is about to do and what it will cost in time, resolution, or bytes.

rules.name: The Hit Shape Rule
rules.body: Any target whose ink does not fill its frame — glyphs, outlines, dashed boxes, caption text — must declare an explicit rectangular content shape. This has caused four separate untappable controls in this codebase.

rules.name: The Consequence Rule
rules.body: A destructive confirmation lists three plain sentences: what is destroyed, what it takes to undo it, and what is not affected. The last line is what makes the tap safe to judge one-handed.

rules.name: The 9 Point Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing renders below 9pt at any text size. A deliberate departure from the platform's 11pt floor, taken because the instrument's density is the design and a uniform 11pt would rewrite it — but 6pt and 7pt captions were not density, they were unreadable. Enforced inside LG.Font, so a call site cannot opt out by passing a smaller number.

rules.name: The Growing Control Rule
rules.body: A control that stacks text sets minHeight, never a fixed height. Identical at the default size; at large sizes the control grows instead of clipping the words inside it. The 76pt primary action is the case that proves it — a fixed height clips the preflight line, which is the sentence saying what the action costs.

rules.name: The Reduce Motion Rule
rules.body: Reduce Motion is about the vestibular system, not about stillness. What goes is travel, scale and spring — sheets fade in place instead of rising, the settings screen crossfades instead of pushing, the hub's spokes keep their staggered sequence but lose the scale-up, and the pairing dot rests at the midpoint of its wire instead of crossing it. What stays is anything that would otherwise state something false: the spinner keeps turning, because a frozen one says the Mac stopped answering and nothing measured that. Every loop routes through LG.Motion.loop / linearLoop, which return nil under the setting so withAnimation lands on the resting state in one step.

dos: Do derive every displayed condition from a measured value, through Condition.from(...), so the label and the numbers cannot disagree.
Do print an em dash in Text Disabled for any value the host has not reported, at the size the real value will occupy.
Do reserve Held Cyan (#6BC7E8) for state the user created — held modifiers, active selection, focused field, Claude — and Reachable Jade / Degraded Sodium / Lost Clay for what the Mac is doing.
Do set every measured value, unit, path, key, and command in mono, and every sentence in sans.
Do give each primary action a mono-caps sub-label stating its cost (540P · SOFT TEXT UNTIL IT RECOVERS).
Do name the failure with its address and verdict — list both transports, their results, and the time of last contact rather than one word for "offline".
Do add an explicit rectangular content shape to any glyph-only, outline-only, or caption-sized target.
Do separate surfaces with a 1pt hairline (#1A1E24 inside a group, #262B33 at a container edge, #2E343D on an interactive edge) and a tonal step.
Do hold layout with a dashed rule or em dash so nothing reflows when a value arrives.
Do keep every tappable control at 44pt or larger, and place destructive taps a full row away from irreversible ones.
Do suppress ambient animation while video is live — pass animated: false the way ConditionDot does on the remote screen.
Do keep motion at 120–180 ms for state changes; the only longer motions are the hub's 0.28s spring with an 18ms per-spoke stagger and the deliberately slow ambient loops on screens with no picture.
donts: Don't add a shadow, blur, or glassmorphic material. Depth is tone plus hairline, and the app has zero shadow calls today.
Don't introduce a light mode or branch on colorScheme. ScreenBody pins .preferredColorScheme(.dark) and the palette assumes it.
Don't use a signal color decoratively, or use cyan for a machine condition. A new color must declare which of the two voices it belongs to.
Don't render a chat bubble, avatar, or typing-dot animation in the Claude panel. Prose runs the full measure under a label.
Don't show a bare spinner in place of a value or a named step. Four named steps with real detail beat one indeterminate arc.
Don't collapse distinct failures into one message. A timeout, a refused connection, a missing permission, and a sleeping Mac are four states with four answers.
Don't wrap code or a diff. Scroll it horizontally; wrapped code lies about indentation and truncated code lies outright.

Don't hard-code a new hex literal at a call site. Seven already exist outside the token file (#C9A468, #C3C8D0, #A8AEB8, #0B0E12, #0D1014, #1E242C, #060709); they are drift, not precedent — add the token instead.
Don't put an oversized decorative layer in a ZStack as a sibling. Anything wider than the phone goes in .background(alignment:), or it resizes the whole screen.
Don't use dashes decoratively. A dashed stroke means unmeasured, pending, or unselected, and it resolves to solid when the thing becomes real.
Don't attach two .sheet modifiers to one view — SwiftUI honors only the first. Move the second onto a child.
